solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Expected night of fine dancing (2,3,6)

indicatorNotes.dancing: letters that dance move about into a new order

annotation.surface: A festive evening of good dancing that everyone has been looking forward to.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is three plain words run together; 'night of fine dancing' reads so naturally as a phrase that the letters hide in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from sailing: a ship in the offing is visible out at sea and soon to arrive, so something in the offing is expected shortly.

entries.clue: Drink needed for climb, I believe (6)

indicatorNotes.needed for: the answer's letters are what the phrase needs, sitting inside it

annotation.surface: Someone insisting a drink is needed after a climb.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma and the break between words disguise the run of letters that spans three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly formal: to imbibe is to drink, especially alcohol, from the Latin for soaking up.

entries.clue: Feign ignorance of spin deviously by a deletion (4,1,5,3,2)

indicatorNotes.deviously: the letters take a devious, crooked route into a new order

annotation.surface: Pretending not to notice some sly spin achieved by quietly deleting something.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a comment on political spin doctors, and the deletion is just letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from Nelson putting his telescope to his blind eye at Copenhagen: to turn a blind eye to something is to pretend not to see it.

entries.clue: Be surprised, on the sea, at waves (3,4,3)

indicatorNotes.waves: letters that wave about are disturbed into a new order

annotation.surface: A sailor astonished by the waves out at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Waves' belongs so well with 'sea' that it hides its job as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: you promise to eat your hat if something happens, so having to do it means being surprised by the outcome.

entries.clue: Female pupils who were at the school, their links ending in time? (4)

blocks.clueFragment: pupils who were at the school

annotation.surface: Former schoolgirls whose ties to the old school are fading with time.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a fob is a chain whose links end in a timepiece, the pocket watch. 'Their' refers back to the fobs themselves.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a fob chain's links end at a pocket watch, the thing that tells the time.

entries.clue: In charge of key areas of expertise, they coolly cover a lot of ground (9)

annotation.definition: they coolly cover a lot of ground
annotation.surface: Calm experts in charge of key areas, covering a wide range of subjects.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition reads as praise for unflappable experts; 'coolly' is literal, since icefields are cold.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: icefields are vast frozen expanses, so they cover a lot of ground, and coldly at that.

entries.clue: Like top medal? Indoor swimmer lacks force (7)

indicatorNotes.lacks: the swimmer is missing a letter

blocks.note: a goldfish swims in a bowl indoors

annotation.surface: A sports report comparing an indoor swimmer's medal hopes with how hard they push.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indoor swimmer' sounds like an athlete in a pool; it is a pet in a bowl.
annotation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means 'somewhat like', so goldish is like gold, the top medal; the question mark flags the jokey word.

entries.clue: Instrument sometimes malfunctioning — I don’t know what to say (11)

indicatorNotes.malfunctioning: a malfunctioning word has its letters working in the wrong order

blocks.clueFragment: I don’t know what to say
blocks.note: er, the noise of someone lost for words

annotation.surface: Someone baffled by a gadget that only works some of the time.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash makes the last phrase look like the speaker's shrug; it is ER, the hesitation sound.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a seismometer is a scientific instrument that measures earthquakes.

entries.clue: Rest days quiet: group of Swedes with a small drink (9)

blocks.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

annotation.surface: A quiet weekend with a Swedish band and a small drink.
annotation.walkthrough: SHABBATOT is the Hebrew plural of Shabbat, the Jewish sabbath; the wordplay builds it piece by piece so it can be trusted.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign plural: Shabbatot are sabbaths, the Jewish weekly days of rest.

entries.clue: With reserve forces finally leaving island in the Med (5)

indicatorNotes.leaving: that letter goes away from the island

annotation.surface: Reserve military forces pulling out of a Mediterranean island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reserve forces' looks like one military phrase; 'reserve' belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Acting icily means with cold reserve, keeping people at a distance.

entries.clue: Error stopping out to lunch — I mostly steer clear of port (9)

indicatorNotes.stopping: the error stops up the middle of the other word
indicatorNotes.mostly: the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: OG = own goal, a footballing error
SHUN (steer clear of) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A sailor confessing to a lunchtime slip while giving a port a wide berth.
annotation.walkthrough: An own goal (OG) is a standard crossword error. 'Steer clear of port' reads as navigation, but 'port' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Mogadishu, capital of Somalia, is a port on the Indian Ocean.

entries.clue: Circulating a rude meme, briefly, is no crime (12)

indicatorNotes.Circulating: the letters go round into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone insisting that sharing an offensive internet joke isn't against the law.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a defence plea; the words 'is no' are fodder, and the anagram swallows most of the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A misdemeanour is a minor crime, a lesser offence in law.

entries.clue: After time, rebuke makes you visibly upset (7)

blocks.note: to give someone an earful is to scold them

annotation.surface: A telling-off that eventually brings you to tears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After time' puts the rebuke after the T. An earful is informal for a sharp scolding.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone tearful has tears showing, so their upset is visible.

entries.clue: Courses dealing with history (6)

annotation.definitionNote: plural 'courses' for a singular meal: a repast is made of courses

blocks.note: re = regarding, as in memo headers

annotation.surface: A prospectus of university courses on history.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Courses' looks academic, next to 'history'; here it means courses of a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, and the courses served together make one up.

entries.clue: Stand in garden back at doctor’s getting stuck into a authoritative book (4,5)

indicatorNotes.back: AT and DR are read backwards
indicatorNotes.getting stuck into: those letters are pushed inside the book

blocks.note: a bible is the authoritative book on a subject
AT DR reversed gives RDTA, stuck into BI-BLE

annotation.surface: A garden stand being wedged into a reference book at the doctor's.
annotation.walkthrough: The printed 'a authoritative' reads oddly but the blocks work regardless: BI(RDTA)BLE. A bird table is a raised platform for feeding garden birds.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a bird table is a stand in a garden where food is put out for birds.

entries.clue: Taking step to overcome article from Paris Match not being original (7)

blocks.note: le is French for 'the'; Paris Match is a French magazine

annotation.surface: A French magazine accused of copying rather than taking bold steps.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: leaping over something is taking a step, a big one, to overcome it.
annotation.definitionFit: Leaping is springing over an obstacle, a step taken to overcome it.

entries.clue: Nearly all go up quietly to get trophy (5)

indicatorNotes.Nearly all: keep all but the last letter

blocks.note: SCALE (go up) without its last letter

annotation.surface: Climbing a mountain quietly to claim a prize.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a climber claiming a summit; the trophy is a victim's scalp.
annotation.definitionFit: A scalp was taken as a war trophy, and by extension a scalp is any notable victory or defeated rival.

entries.clue: Smart, in light clothes, following bishop (6)

indicatorNotes.clothes: the light is wrapped round IN
indicatorNotes.following: that result comes after the bishop

annotation.surface: A clergyman dressed smartly in light-coloured clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smart' and 'light clothes' suggest fashion; 'clothes' is a verb, RAY clothing IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: brainy and smart both mean clever.

entries.clue: Holding note, I play it quivering with pathos (8)

indicatorNotes.Holding: the anagrammed letters hold the note
indicatorNotes.quivering: the letters shake into a new order

annotation.surface: A violinist holding a long note, playing it with a tremulous vibrato.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a musician's direction; 'quivering' is vibrato in the story and the anagram signal in the parse.
annotation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that arouses pity, so doing something pitiably is doing it with pathos.

entries.clue: Brief commotion follows on the wagon carrying English man wrongly imprisoned (7)

indicatorNotes.Brief: cuts the last letter of FUSS
indicatorNotes.follows: to follow is to come after, so FUS is placed after DREY
indicatorNotes.carrying: a thing carrying a load has it inside, so DRY holds the E within it

blocks.note: on the wagon = not drinking alcohol

annotation.surface: A brief fuss as a teetotal Englishman, falsely jailed, is carted off in a wagon.
annotation.walkthrough: Alfred Dreyfus was the French army officer wrongly convicted of treason in 1894. 'Wagon' reads as a prison van but means sobriety.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Dreyfus is the most famous victim of wrongful imprisonment, the subject of the Dreyfus affair.

entries.clue: Rich commotion below watering hole? (4-2-2)

indicatorNotes.below: in a down answer, the commotion sits under the well

blocks.note: a well is a hole for drawing water

annotation.surface: A rowdy scene beneath a village pub.
annotation.walkthrough: A watering hole is slang for a pub; the question mark says to read it literally, as a hole giving water.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the well-to-do are wealthy, so well-to-do means rich.

entries.clue: One hundred percent inflation which puts paid to spring work (4,4,4,4,4)

blocks.note: a swell is an inflation, a swelling
to put paid to is to end
a spring is a well of water

annotation.surface: Total inflation that wipes out any work in spring, an economist's gloomy forecast.
annotation.walkthrough: The chunks are cut in unexpected places: ALL + SWELL, not ALL'S + WELL. 'Work' is the whole definition, the Shakespeare comedy.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: All's Well That Ends Well is a play by Shakespeare, a literary work.

entries.clue: Sea creature emerging from short grass with small boy (7)

indicatorNotes.short: cuts the last letter of NARK

blocks.note: NARK (grass, informer) without its last letter
Hal, the pet form of Henry

annotation.surface: A creature appearing out of a lawn alongside a small boy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is a British slang verb and noun for informing to the police; a nark is an informer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the narwhal is an Arctic whale whose male grows a long spiral tusk.

entries.clue: Turned to large bottles originally holding sauce (8)

indicatorNotes.bottles: BECAME L bottles up the letter

blocks.note: a thing that turned to ice became ice
first letter of holding, bottled inside BEC-AMEL

annotation.surface: Someone turning to big bottles that held a sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' is a verb, and 'holding' only supplies its H; read as a noun and a participle they paint a kitchen scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: béchamel is the classic French white sauce of butter, flour and milk.

entries.clue: Chap let down when trading heads for complimentary post? (3,4)

indicatorNotes.trading heads: the two words swap their first letters

blocks.note: to fail someone is to let them down

annotation.surface: A man disappointed when his job swap brings only praise in the letterbox.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heads' are first letters. 'Complimentary' means praising, not free, which the question mark hints at.
annotation.definitionFit: Fan mail is admiring letters sent to a celebrity, post full of compliments.

entries.clue: Leave coat with Allen, perhaps (8)

blocks.note: an animal's fur is its coat
Lough Allen is a lake in Ireland; lough is Irish for lake

annotation.surface: Leaving your coat with someone called Allen.
annotation.walkthrough: Allen looks like a person's name; it is Lough Allen, an Irish lake, and 'perhaps' signals an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A furlough is a leave of absence, especially for soldiers.

entries.clue: I’ll formally honour South African instrumentalist (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a phrase a saluter would say, standing for the noun
annotation.surface: A South African musician promising to pay a formal tribute.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken in the first person by the saluter, which makes it hard to recognise as a definition at all.
annotation.definitionFit: A saluter is one who salutes, a formal mark of honour, so the saluter can say 'I'll formally honour'.

entries.clue: Confession to murder when cycling in Hebridean location (5)

indicatorNotes.when cycling: letters move from the front round to the back

blocks.note: I and S move round to the end

annotation.surface: A murderer confesses while out on a bicycle in the Scottish islands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' suggests a bike ride; it means rotating letters. Lewis is the northern part of the largest island of the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Lewis is in the Outer Hebrides, so it is a Hebridean location.

entries.clue: Burning of billet every so often in base (7)

indicatorNotes.every so often: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

annotation.surface: A firewood log burning intermittently in a grate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Billet' looks like soldiers' lodgings; here it is simply the source of letters, and 'base' means low-minded.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic word: unnoble means ignoble, and base means morally low, so the two match.

entries.clue: Rise early to get abreast of mischief? (2,2,4,3,4)

blocks.note: be up with = keep abreast of; a lark = a mischievous prank

annotation.surface: Getting up at dawn to keep an eye on the children's pranks.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: 'be up with' as keeping level, and 'lark' as a prank rather than the bird.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom compares early risers to the lark, which sings at dawn; read literally it means keeping pace with a prank.

entries.clue: Bank at liberty to delay fine (4)

indicatorNotes.to delay: the F is put off, moved to the end

blocks.note: f = fine, the pencil grade; the F of FREE is delayed to the end

annotation.surface: A bank letting a customer put off paying a fine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' reads as the financial kind, and 'delay fine' as late payment; it is a sandbank.
annotation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or sand near the water's surface, which is a bank in the nautical sense.

entries.clue: Met prisoner, greatly enthused (8)

annotation.surface: A police officer from the Met thrilled by a prisoner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Met' looks like London's Metropolitan Police; it is the past tense of meet.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal: to powwow is to hold a meeting or discussion, so powwowed means met to confer.

entries.clue: Avert battle over shed (4,3)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down answer, WAR sits above DOFF

blocks.note: to doff is to take off, shed

annotation.surface: Preventing a fight over a garden shed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a noun, the object of the battle; it is a verb, to doff.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ward off a danger is to avert it.

entries.clue: Demand pulling broadcast (5)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: broadcasting is sending out sound, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: draught = pulling, as a draught horse pulls a cart

annotation.surface: A demand to pull a programme off the air.
annotation.walkthrough: British spelling separates draught (pulling, and a current of air) from draft (a bank order); they sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A bank draft is a written demand for payment, an order drawn on a bank.

entries.clue: Back transatlantic allies fronting hotel chain (5,4)

indicatorNotes.fronting: the allies go in front of the hotel

blocks.note: hind = back, as in hind legs
the UK and US, across the Atlantic
H = hotel in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Supporting a transatlantic partnership that leads a hotel chain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hotel chain' looks like one business phrase; the H is from 'hotel' and 'chain' means a mountain range.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Hindu Kush is a mountain chain in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

entries.clue: Gold’s wartime place as standard with money, ultimately (8)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letter of money

annotation.surface: Gold's place as the monetary standard during the war.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface talks about the gold standard; Gold was a code name for one of the D-Day landing beaches.
annotation.definitionFit: Gold Beach was one of the five Allied landing beaches in Normandy on D-Day, 1944.

entries.clue: Fare that’s unearthly blocks Kitty visiting Oscar (6,6)

indicatorNotes.blocks: ET sits in the middle of the kitty, blocking it
indicatorNotes.visiting: AT: someone visiting is at a place

blocks.note: the kitty or pot of money
ET, the extraterrestrial, is unearthly; it goes inside JACK-POT
O = Oscar in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Supernatural food getting in the way of a cat named Kitty visiting her friend Oscar.
annotation.walkthrough: Kitty and Oscar look like two pets. A jacket potato is a British term for a baked potato cooked in its skin.
annotation.definitionFit: Fare means food, and a jacket potato is a common dish of it.

entries.clue: Carmen’s admirer say, old, a past monarch (5-4)

blocks.note: per = a, as in 'ten pounds a head'

annotation.surface: An admirer of Carmen, perhaps a former king.
annotation.walkthrough: Carmen is Bizet's opera, not a woman; 'say' marks an opera-goer as one example of her admirers.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: someone who admires the opera Carmen is, say, an opera-goer.

entries.clue: Little matters when trained army falls short of ammunition initially (5,3)

indicatorNotes.trained: the letters are drilled into a new order
indicatorNotes.initially: takes the first letter of ammunition

blocks.note: lose an A, the first letter of ammunition

annotation.surface: A trained army, lacking ammunition, finds that only little things matter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trained army' looks like a military unit; 'trained' is the anagram signal and 'matters' is a noun in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Small fry are young fish, and so unimportant people or things: little matters.

entries.clue: Crawled, possibly, out of marsh before the end (4)

annotation.surface: Someone crawling out of a swamp just before the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crawled' suggests hands and knees; it is the front crawl, a swimming stroke, and 'possibly' marks the example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: someone who did the front crawl swam.

entries.clue: Henry and I open a box, trembling, fearing the unknown (10)

annotation.definitionNote: gerund phrase for a noun: xenophobia is fearing foreigners

indicatorNotes.trembling: letters that tremble are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: H = henry, the unit of inductance

annotation.surface: Two people nervously opening a mystery box.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is Pandora's box; the 'unknown' in the definition is the stranger or foreigner.
annotation.definitionFit: Xenophobia, from Greek xenos (stranger), is fear of foreigners, of people unknown to one.

entries.clue: Good seaside speciality found by the French visitor to Cornwall? (7)

blocks.note: seaside rock, a stick of hard candy sold at British resorts

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker in Cornwall finding good local seaside treats and French people.
annotation.walkthrough: Grockle is West Country slang, mildly scornful, for a tourist; the question mark says Cornwall is one example of where it is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: in Devon and Cornwall a grockle is a holidaymaker, a visitor to the area.

entries.clue: Having zip fastener, not secure, get one caught (9)

indicatorNotes.not: FAST is removed from the fastener

annotation.surface: A jacket with a zip that won't stay done up, so it gets snagged.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all about zips; 'zip' in the definition means vigour.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal: zip is vim and vigour, like the zipping sound of something moving fast, so a person with plenty of it is full of go.

entries.clue: One going right around yellow dog that’s dangerous? (7)

blocks.note: or = gold or yellow in heraldry
a biting dog is a dangerous one

annotation.surface: Someone making a full circle round a vicious yellow dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right around' sounds like walking round the dog; it means a full orbit.
annotation.definitionFit: An orbiter, such as a satellite or spacecraft, goes right around a planet.

entries.clue: Ordered to impound expensive car — one about to cause obstruction (9)

indicatorNotes.to impound: BADE locks the other letters up inside it

blocks.note: ca = circa, about; RR I CA all go inside BA-DE

annotation.surface: Police told to seize a luxury car, one said to be blocking the road.
annotation.walkthrough: The contents are three chunks in a row: BA(RR-I-CA)DE.
annotation.definitionFit: A barricade is a barrier put up to block a street, an obstruction.

entries.clue: Our meal given scattering of French dressing (9)

indicatorNotes.scattering: the letters are strewn into a new order

annotation.surface: Our dinner served with a sprinkle of French dressing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French dressing' reads as vinaigrette; 'of French' gives DE, and the dressing is a different French one.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: rémoulade is a French mayonnaise-based dressing with herbs and capers.

entries.clue: Stamen, tall, keeps bearing catkins (7)

indicatorNotes.keeps: the phrase keeps the answer inside it

annotation.surface: A botanist describing a tall plant with long stamens and catkins.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word is botanical, so the hidden word blends in. An ament is a catkin.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical word: ament is botany's term for a catkin, and amental plants bear them.

entries.clue: War verses repeated do haunt the memory of irregular (6,3,6,5)

indicatorNotes.repeated: a thing repeated happens again, so the word 'do' is written out a second time
indicatorNotes.irregular: the letters are put in an irregular order

anagram.fodder: DO DO HAUNT THE MEMORY OF

annotation.surface: Lines of war poetry, read again and again, that linger in the memory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' seems to hang off the end, as though the soldiers were irregulars; it is the anagram signal. Wilfred Owen wrote the poem in 1917.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Anthem for Doomed Youth is Wilfred Owen's First World War sonnet, verses about war.

entries.clue: Storyteller outspoken in support of software user (7)

indicatorNotes.outspoken: spoken out loud, so the word is heard
indicatorNotes.in support of: in a down answer, the storyteller sits under the software, holding it up

blocks.note: an app is a piece of software
a storyteller tells fibs, so is a liar

annotation.surface: A blunt-speaking writer who backs a particular computer program.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Software user' looks like one phrase; 'software' is APP and 'user' alone is the definition. Storyteller is a euphemism for liar.
annotation.definitionFit: An applier is one who applies something, putting it to use, so a user.

entries.clue: Works round Brussels against almost everyone else? (7)

indicatorNotes.almost: the last letter of REST is dropped

blocks.note: the EU is based in Brussels

annotation.surface: A Brussels circular opposed by nearly every other nation.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark covers Brussels standing for the EU; the surface suggests European politics.
annotation.definitionFit: A French loan: an artist's oeuvres are their works.

entries.clue: City no longer on the up, I would add a car crash? (6)

indicatorNotes.on the up: in a down answer, going up means reading backwards

blocks.note: a PS, postscript, is what you add to a letter

annotation.surface: A city in decline, and, adds the commentator, a car crash of a place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No longer' says the ancient city is gone. RTA is British officialese for a road traffic accident.
annotation.definitionFit: Sparta was the ancient Greek city-state famed for its warriors, a city no longer in its old form.

entries.clue: Change of direction involving French in front (6)

indicatorNotes.involving: VEER takes EN into its middle

blocks.note: to veer is to change direction
en = 'in' in French, placed inside V-EER

annotation.surface: A sudden change of course that brings the French in at the front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French in front' sounds like a battle line; 'French' alone gives EN.
annotation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin surface layer, so a false front hiding what lies beneath.

entries.clue: Charter maybe heading for Greece — quickly boards at the front (3,4)

indicatorNotes.heading for: takes the first letter of Greece
indicatorNotes.at the front: the boarding phrase is placed before the G

annotation.surface: A charter flight to Greece, passengers hurrying aboard at the front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charter' is a charter plane in the surface; it is something that makes the charts, a hit record.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: a charter is something that gets into the charts, and a pop song may do that.

entries.clue: Grand old bovine philosopher promoting pleasure (8)

blocks.note: epic = grand, on a large scale
the urus, or aurochs, is an extinct wild ox

annotation.surface: A great old cow-like thinker who preached enjoyment.
annotation.walkthrough: URUS is the extinct wild ox, a word crosswords lean on.
annotation.definitionFit: Epicurus, the Greek philosopher, taught that pleasure, understood as calm and freedom from pain, is the highest good.

entries.clue: Starve, presumably, without right inspiration (5)

indicatorNotes.without: an old sense: outside, so EAT O goes round R

blocks.note: to starve is, presumably, to eat O, nothing

annotation.surface: An artist starving for want of the right inspiration.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking'; here it is the old sense 'outside'. Erato is the Muse of love poetry.
annotation.definitionFit: Erato was one of the nine Muses, who inspire poets, so a Muse stands for inspiration.

entries.clue: Plan that’s sound if unhealthy (6)

blocks.note: a crafty scheme, in British schoolboy slang
the whistling breath of the sick

annotation.surface: A plan that looks healthy but isn't.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as 'healthy', the opposite of 'unhealthy'; it is a noise.
annotation.definitionFit: Wheeze is British schoolboy slang for a clever plan; it is also the rasping sound of laboured breathing.

entries.clue: Pressure, not unknown in pump, causing crack (4)

indicatorNotes.not: 'not unknown' means without the unknown, so the Z is removed from QUIZ
indicatorNotes.in: the pressure letter is put in where the Z was, taking its place

blocks.note: to pump someone is to quiz them
z, a mathematical unknown, is taken out

annotation.surface: A pump with pressure unknown, causing a crack in the pipe.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is plumbing, but 'pump' is questioning and 'crack' is a joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a quip, a short witty remark.

entries.clue: Educated woman dramatically grabbing a side dish (5)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: RITA grabs A and holds it inside

blocks.note: Educating Rita, Willy Russell's play about a woman seeking education

annotation.surface: A learned actress snatching food from the table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dramatically' points to a play: Rita is the student in Educating Rita.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: raita is an Indian side dish of yogurt with cucumber or mint.

entries.clue: Ode in praise of pre-race favourite recited? Exactly (2,1,4)

indicatorNotes.recited: a recited poem is heard, so its title is heard

blocks.clueFragment: Ode in praise of pre-race favourite recited
blocks.note: an ode addressed to the hare, favourite before the race with the tortoise

annotation.surface: A poem honouring the favourite before a race, read aloud.
annotation.walkthrough: Odes are often titled 'To a ...', like Burns's To a Mouse. The hare was the favourite before Aesop's race with the tortoise, which it lost.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: matching something to a hair means matching it precisely, down to the width of a hair.

entries.clue: Obscure answer given by foolish class (9)

blocks.note: a rate is a class, as in first-rate

annotation.surface: An unclear answer from a silly class of pupils.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective describing the answer; it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To adumbrate, from Latin umbra (shade), is to overshadow or obscure.

entries.clue: Express on European railroad stops presidential transport (3,5,3)

indicatorNotes.stops: FORCE stops up the gap in the middle

blocks.note: to air a view is to express it
to railroad someone is to force them; it goes between AIR and ONE

annotation.surface: A European express train halted to make way for the president.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Express' and 'railroad' are both verbs here, though the surface makes them a train and a track.
annotation.definitionFit: Air Force One is the call sign of the aircraft carrying the President of the United States.

entries.clue: This kipper is off! (11)

blocks.note: the surface serves a smoked herring; the setter means someone who kips, a sleeper
the surface says the fish has gone bad; the setter means the sleeper has set off walking

annotation.surface: A complaint about a smoked fish gone bad.
annotation.walkthrough: The kipper looks like the smoked herring and 'off' like spoiled; kip is British slang for sleep, so a kipper is a sleeper, and 'off' means wandering away.
annotation.definitionFit: A sleepwalker is a sleeper who gets up and walks off while still asleep.
